title: The Moon May Have Been Created in Just Five Hours - Nautilus
gist: Computational modeling by University of Arizona and Southwest Research Institute researchers suggests the moon could have formed in as little as five hours from the impact between Earth and the Mars-sized body Theia some 4.5 billion years ago.

insights.claim: A new study suggests the moon could have formed in as little as five hours following the giant impact, rather than over an extended accretion period.
insights.so_what: A near-instantaneous formation timescale changes what lunar sample chemistry should look like, which bears on how upcoming lunar missions are targeted.
insights.quote: A new study suggests the moon could’ve formed in as little as five hours.
insights.locator: The next time you’re getting a quote
insights.speaker: David Nield

insights.claim: Researchers from the University of Arizona and the Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) used computational modeling of the roughly 4.5-billion-year-old collision between Earth and the Mars-sized object Theia.
insights.so_what: SwRI and Arizona are the institutional centers for giant-impact modeling; their simulation results set the priors that lunar mission science is interpreted against.
insights.locator: Researchers from the University of Arizona
insights.speaker: David Nield

insights.claim: For a unique, unobservable, one-off event like the moon-forming impact, computational modeling rather than observation is the primary evidentiary method, so conclusions move as compute and model fidelity improve.
insights.so_what: Expect origin-of-the-moon claims to keep revising with compute; treat any single simulation headline as provisional.
insights.locator: Researchers from the University of Arizona and the Southwest Research Institute
insights.speaker: David Nield
